title: Cortex deploy-parity operands
description:
The two values a box compared to decide `deploy_parity.match`, plus the verdict it drew from them. `deploy_parity` answers whether the running process matches its source; this answers WHY, so a consumer can tell a real drift from an unknowable one instead of reading a bare false. Published under the health payload's `extra` (canonically `extra.parity_operands`), never as a second top-level field. Status: DRAFT v0 — introduced in contracts-v0.4.0; bump $id on breaking changes.

This schema exists because three boxes independently grew the same object with different vocabularies and different semantics for the same field names. It is normative about all four:

1. BASIS names the CONCEPT compared, not the box's local variable names. Producers previously emitted six strings for two concepts (deploy_stamp_vs_checkout / boot_sha_vs_checkout_head / boot_sha_vs_live_head, and built_bundle_vs_live_bundle / boot_bundle_vs_disk_bundle / boot_bundle_vs_live_bundle).
2. VERDICT is operand equality and nothing else. A box that also tracks whether its working tree is dirty reports that in `tree_clean`; folding it into the verdict made one box's `false` mean something the others' `false` did not.
3. COMMIT SHA operands are compared strictly, so they must be full 40-character SHAs. Prefix comparison was a workaround for one box stamping a short SHA, and it silently accepts a 7-character collision.
4. COMPLETE means both operand values were readable. It is not a statement about whether some unrelated probe (git porcelain) succeeded, and it is not implied by which branch the producer took.

basis.description: Which concept was compared. `commit_sha`: the commit the running process baked at boot against the commit its checkout is on now. `bundle_hash`: a content hash of the artifact the process is running against the artifact on disk. `none`: no operand pair was obtainable, so no comparison happened — `complete` must then be false and `verdict` null.

expected.description: The reference side: what the process SHOULD be running.

name.description: The producer's own label for this operand, for humans reading a report. Free-form and never keyed on by a consumer; `basis` is the machine-readable identity.

value.description: The compared value, or null when it could not be read. A `commit_sha` basis requires the full 40-character lowercase SHA — normalize a short SHA before comparing rather than comparing by prefix.

source.description: Where the value came from (an env var name, a file path, a git command), so a wrong value can be traced to what produced it.

actual.description: The observed side: what the process IS running. Same field rules as `expected`.

complete.description: True when BOTH operand values are non-null, and therefore a comparison was possible. False means the answer is unknown, not negative. Do not set this from the success of an unrelated probe, and do not hardcode it per branch.

self_referential.description: True when the two operands are derived from the same artifact, so the comparison can only ever agree. A self-referential comparison is not evidence and must carry a null verdict — this flag exists so a consumer can refuse to count it as a pass. Note the casing: snake_case, like every other field here.

tree_clean.description: Whether the served working tree has no uncommitted changes, when the producer can tell; null when it cannot. Reported ALONGSIDE the verdict, never folded into it: a box serving a dirty tree at the expected commit has verdict true and tree_clean false, and a consumer that cares about tree state reads this field.

verdict.description: Whether `expected.value` and `actual.value` are equal, by exact string comparison. Null — never false — when `complete` is false or `self_referential` is true, because an unknowable comparison is not a failed one. Carries no other meaning: not tree cleanliness, not staleness, not liveness.

note.description: Free prose for a human reading a drift report: what was missing, or what a false verdict implies for this box. Never parsed.
